title: Community-mean field-decay model outputs and composition regressions for Dutch roadside cuttings
citation: Schaffers, A.P., Vesseur, M.C. & Sýkora, K.V. (1998). Effects of delayed hay removal on the nutrient balance of roadside plant communities. Journal of Applied Ecology, 35, 166–174.
geography: Netherlands; roadside grassland plots in a 1993 field campaign
field_period: 24 May–6 July 1993; seven grassland plots had 5–6 week exposure, contrasting grass-heath plot had 4 weeks
license: No explicit open license identified on accessible article record; concise table facts transcribed with full attribution.
method: Table 4 values are reported community means of fitted/model-estimated remaining fractions and asymptotic parameters. Table 5 coefficients are source-reported regressions. Values are transcribed as printed; decimal points normalize the source's decimal-point glyphs; no parameter conversion or fit is performed.
equations: Plot/community field decay: Y(t)=a+(1-a)*exp(-k*t), where Y is remaining fraction; a is asymptotic remaining fraction; k is week^-1.
scope: Phase 2 field delay/decomposition before biomass removal. This does not describe ensiling, bunker storage, indoor storage, or anaerobic degradation.
limitations: Dutch roadside-cutting field experiment in 1993; cut material was left in field litterbags for up to six weeks. This is field-delay/decomposition evidence, not bunker ensiling, warehouse storage, or GreenHub feed-specific kinetics. No runtime mapping or GreenHub default activation.
Table 4 values are model-estimated community means and are not raw litterbag replicates.
Table 5 regressions were based on seven grassland plots, with the grass-heath (Ericion) plot excluded initially; article warns of extrapolation beyond the observed C:N range.
The potassium regressions were not statistically significant, are described as poor/may be unjustified, and have no satisfactory asymptotic fit.
The source has no direct GreenHub feed, storage, leachate, emissions, protein, COD or methane measurements.
This extract complements the existing Table 1/Table 3 plot-level dataset; do not double-count fitted parameters or treat alternative Table 4/5 regressions as independent observations.
